Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Pinnacle Bancorp Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, ladies and gentlemen, this conference is being recorded. I will now advise you that if you have any questions or would like operator assistance, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. Otherwise, please sit back and enjoy the presentation.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review Pinnacle Bancorp's results for the Q3 2024. With me this morning are David Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Reynolds, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Risk Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to David Thompson.

David Thompson:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Pinnacle Bancorp delivered solid performance in the Q3 2024, demonstrating the strength of our diversified business model and our commitment to serving our customers.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on:
1. Enhancing customer experience
2. Driving operational efficiency
3. Investing in strategic growth initiatives
4. Maintaining strong capital levels.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights on the macroeconomic outlook and its impact, NII trends year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter growth or decline, cost of deposits including average rates and competitive pressures, and key assumptions underlying our guidance.

On the macroeconomic front, we're cautiously optimistic with global GDP growth projected at around 3.1% for 2024, reflecting resilience in the U.S. at 2.6% annualized in Q2 driven by strong consumer spending and a steady labor market with unemployment at 4.1%. We're anticipating 75 basis points of Fed rate cuts, bringing the funds rate to 4.25-4.50% by year-end, which supports our net interest income while we navigate softer growth in Europe at 0.8% and mixed signals in Asia-Pacific. This backdrop bolsters our loan growth at 5.2% year-over-year, particularly in commercial real estate outside of office, with strict LTV caps under 65%, and drives noninterest income through capital markets strength.

Turning to NII trends, we saw robust year-over-year expansion reflecting higher-for-longer rates, with our net interest margin improving meaningfully, fueled by asset repricing and steady deposit franchise. Quarter-over-quarter, growth moderated due to seasonal factors but core trends remain solid, supported by hedging strategies.

Regarding cost of deposits, our average rates have risen in line with betas around 42% since the hiking cycle began, but our mix remains low-cost heavy with non-interest-bearing at 32% and competitive positioning below peers. We're countering fintech pressures through pricing analytics and innovative products.

Finally, our full-year 2025 guidance assumes a soft landing with GDP at 1.8-2.2%, three Fed cuts, loan growth of 4.5-5.5%, and ROTCE in the mid-teens, embedding conservatism across macro, credit, and balance sheet levers.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Reynolds to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, David, and good morning. Pinnacle Bancorp reported net income of $1.4 billion for the Q3 2024, or $2.15 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 9% driven by higher interest rates and loan growth. Let me unpack this in more detail, as NII remains the bedrock of our earnings profile. In Q3, we delivered NII of $13.2 billion, up 9.1% year-over-year from $12.1 billion in Q3 2023, though up a more modest 3.1% quarter-over-quarter from $12.8 billion in Q2. The year-over-year growth stems from the sustained higher-for-longer rate environment since the Fed's hiking cycle began in early 2022. Our NIM expanded to 3.20% in Q3 from 2.95% a year ago, a 25 basis point gain, powered by loan yields averaging 5.85% across the portfolio, up from 5.45%, thanks to repricing on variable-rate commercial loans linked to SOFR and Prime. C&I lending grew 8% to $285 billion with tighter spreads in a resilient economy, while consumer lending balances rose 6% to $210 billion with yields at 7.2% on higher revolving utilization.

Funding costs rose with deposit betas at 85% for interest-bearing deposits versus 65% last year, but our core non-interest-bearing demand deposits stayed stable at 28% of total deposits, muting the pass-through. Total deposits expanded 4% year-over-year to $1.05 trillion, aided by digital initiatives like our high-yield savings via the Pinnacle Mobile app, drawing $15 billion in low-cost retail inflows. U.S. operations, 65% of NII, led the growth at the Fed funds rate of 5.25-5.50%; Europe saw 12% local currency growth on ECB rates around 4%; Asia-Pacific lagged at 3% due to yen weakness and deposit competition.

Quarter-over-quarter, the 3.1% rise offset seasonal paydowns in C&I and mortgage pauses at 6.5-7% rates, with core NII up 1.8% excluding a $250 million Q2 securities gain from repositioning legacy MBS into agency floaters. NIM held at 3.20%, though funding costs edged to 2.45% from 2.35%. Our ALM team deployed $10 billion in swaps hedging 40% of floating loans at a 4.75% SOFR floor, lifting our hedge ratio to 55%. The $320 billion securities portfolio duration extended to 4.2 years at 3.8% yields via investment-grade corporates. We've held deposit beta discipline with tiered relationship pricing 20 bps below industry averages, yielding NII sensitivity of +$150 million for a 100 bps rate drop. We guide full-year 2024 NII to $52.5-$53.5 billion, 7-9% growth, NIM at 3.15-3.25%.

This performance ties directly into deposit dynamics. Our total deposit cost averaged 2.45% in Q3, up 28 basis points from Q2's 2.17% and 105 bps from last year's 1.40%, with a 42% beta since March 2022. Non-interest-bearing DDA at 32% of deposits cost just 0.05%, bolstered by $1,200 average treasury fees per relationship. Interest-bearing transaction and savings at 41% rose to 1.92% via tiered 'Pinnacle Elite' products; CDs at 27% hit 4.12%, grown selectively 4% for duration. This is below KBW peers at 2.78% and BofA at 2.62%.

Competitive pressures are intense from fintechs like Ally at 4.20% APY, SoFi 4.50%, Marcus 4.40%, and MMFs at 5.10%, pulling $120 billion industry-wide. In Midwest core markets (65% deposits), urban rivals like Chase push 15-20 bps higher, but rural stickiness keeps beta at 35%; Florida/Texas (20%) average 2.78% amid Regions' specials; California pilots hit 55% beta. We saw 2.1% outflows from MMDA, but LDR at 92%.

Our response includes AI pricing engines with Temenos and FICO, cutting lag 15 days and capping retail beta at 38%; 'Pinnacle LockBox' CDs at 4.25% with swaps; 'Rewards Checking' at 2.75% APY for cross-sells, upping non-interest 8%; commercial campaigns converting outflows to DDA at 22% rate; tokenized deposits for HNW; affinity CDs in Florida at 4.10%, agribusiness loyalty in Midwest at 85% retention. Q4 costs guide to 2.65-2.75%, with lagged beta aiding NIM expansion 10-15 bps on cuts.

Non-interest income was impacted by a modest seasonal dip in investment banking fees amid waiting M&A rebound. We continue to maintain a strong capital position with a CET1 ratio of 11.5%. 

Before opening for Q&A, let me outline our refined full-year 2025 guidance: adjusted EPS $5.85-$6.15, 8-12% over 2024; NII growth 4-6%, non-interest revenue 7-9%, total revenue 5-7%; expenses low-single digits for 58-60% efficiency; ROTCE 14-15%; provisions $950 million-$1.1 billion, NCOs 45-55 bps.

Key assumptions draw from Philadelphia Fed and Bloomberg consensus, stress-tested via CECL and Basel III. Macro: U.S. soft landing, GDP 1.8-2.2%, core PCE 2.3-2.6%, three 25 bps Fed cuts to 4.75-5.00% terminal (75% CME probability), unemployment 4.1-4.3%; NIM 3.25-3.45% with betas 65-75% down, loan yields 5.80-6.00%; ECB two cuts from 4.25-4.50%, BOE steady; resilient U.S. spending on $1.2T savings, Europe energy limits 2-3% loans, Asia ex-China 6-8%.

Balance sheet: loans +4.5-5.5%, C&I/specialty 5-7% with $2B equipment finance via Fundbox; consumer 3% incl. $15B autos; CRE office 12% of loans with <60 bps NCOs, multifamily/industrial LTV<65%; deposits +3-5%, LDR 88-92%, $20B core via Pinnacle Mobile (2.5M MAUs +25%); wholesale to SOFR+25 bps, $10B FHLB rolloff.

Credit: reserves 1.20-1.30x losses, provisions $1.0B; delinquencies consumer 1.8-2.0%, commercial 0.9-1.1%, NCOs 48 bps; +100 bps unemployment stress +15% provisions due to 65% IG corporates, FICO 740+; AI early warning with SymphonyAI cuts delinquencies 20%; HTM yields 4.1%, DV01 <$15M.

Non-interest: fees +7-9%, IB +10-12% on $450M M&A (10% of 2021 peaks), trading flat-+5% (MOVE 110); AUM +8% to $450B, $25B flows via Pinnacle Wealth AI (15% mass-affluent share); payments/cards $1.2B +6%, +9% volumes PSD3 tokenization; minimal crypto <0.5%.

Expenses: +2-4% to $6.8-7.0B, comp flat, tech CapEx 8% ($550M) for AWS migration (70% done, -25% data costs), GenAI fraud ($100M savings, -30% false positives), Plaid/Tink APIs ($200M 2026 revenue); efficiency to 59%, 60% smart branches.

Capital: CET1 11.2-11.5% >10.4% DFAST; $1.5B buybacks (4% shares), dividend +25 bps to $1.48, no SIFI surcharges; embedded finance BNPL for Walmart-like, $10B green bonds tighter spreads.

Risks: inflation delays (-$0.20 EPS), CRE (40% floating mitigant), geopolitics (2% trade loans); upside faster disinflation/M&A. This positions us ahead of peers on ROTCE.

We are pleased with the progress we are making on our strategic initiatives, and we remain confident in our ability to deliver sustainable value for our shareholders.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you have any questions or would like operator assistance, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Mike Mayo with Wells Fargo Securities. Please go ahead.

Mike Mayo:
Good morning. Can you provide some color on NII trends YoY and QoQ growth/decline?

David Thompson:
Good morning, Mike. Happy to elaborate. As Michael detailed, the 9.1% YoY surge and 3.1% QoQ reflect our asset-sensitive stance and hedges, with forward stability into cuts. Our diversified geography and digital deposit growth give us an edge.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Betsy Graseck with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Betsy Graseck:
Good morning. What is your outlook for cost of deposits average rates and competitive pressures?

Michael Reynolds:
Good morning, Betsy. We're guiding modest rises but below peers, leveraging AI pricing and products like LockBox CDs to defend core funding at 65% versus industry 58%, positioning ROATD over 85 bps even as betas normalize.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Gerard Cassidy with RBC Capital Markets. Please go ahead.

Gerard Cassidy:
Good morning. Can you discuss the impact of macroeconomic outlook on your loan portfolio?

Lisa Chen:
Good morning, Gerard. Our portfolio is resilient, with variable-rate exposure and derisking office CRE by 15% QoQ, LTVs under 65%, and AI mitigants keeping delinquencies low. Stress tests confirm CET1 buffer under downside GDP/unemployment scenarios, while ESG lending adds premium yields.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to David Thompson for any closing remarks.

David Thompson:
Thank you for your interest in Pinnacle Bancorp. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
